To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
natural product derived compounds are a promising source of new antibacterial drugs against multi-drug resistant St. aureus infections.
natural product derived compounds have been identified as potent anti-MRSA leads and the SAR studies have revealed the structural requirements for potent activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure activity relationship (SAR) studies and mechanism of action studies of natural product derivatives as anti-MRSA agents.
the discovery and development of novel natural product derivatives as potential anti-MRSA drugs.
the synthesis of novel natural product derived anti-MRSA compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the natural products and their derivatives have been the most promising source of antibacterials and will continue to be so.
natural product derived antibacterials have been found to be promising leads for the discovery of anti-MRSA drugs.
natural product derived compounds are a rich and valuable source of new antibacterial agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
natural products or their derived semisynthic variations can be a promising source of novel anti-MRSA drug candidates with new mechanism of actions.
natural product derived semisynthetics have shown promising in vitro and in vivo anti-MRSA activity.
the natural product-derived compounds have been shown to be promising leads for the development of novel anti-MRSA agents with new mechanism(s) of action.

natural product-derived anti-MRSA agents are a promising lead for further optimization to develop potent and effective drugs.
natural products are a valuable source of antibacterial leads for the development of novel antibacterials with new mechanism of actions.
natural product derived antibacterial agents have a great potential to be used for the treatment of MRSA infections.
